extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent attorneys, and foreign companies seeking patent protection and enforcement in the Russian Federation
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and legal standards for obtaining, prosecuting, enforcing and challenging invention, utility model and design patents in the Russian Federation, including filing routes, examination, nullity, litigation, remedies and administrative/criminal enforcement. Aimed at practitioners and rights-holders operating under Russian law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements for invention patents
rubrics_metrics.description: To be patentable, the claimed invention must be novel and inventive over the prior art and must possess industrial applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty = absolute (any information known to the public in the world before the priority date). Inventiveness = for the specialist the invention does not obviously ensue from the prior art. Industrial applicability = usable in industry, agriculture, public health and other branches; insufficient exemplification (e.g. in chemistry) is a common substantive-examination objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements for utility model patents
rubrics_metrics.description: The claimed utility model must be novel and industrially applicable; utility models do not have to fulfill the 'inventiveness' requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility models are for apparatus-type technical solutions (not processes or many biological products). Prior art for utility models is relative: includes information published worldwide concerning means having the same intended purpose and information about their use in the Russian Federation prior to the priority date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements for design (industrial design) patents
rubrics_metrics.description: A design patent is granted for artistic and design solutions determining the appearance of an article; the claimed design must be novel and original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant features determining aesthetic and/or ergonomic characteristics (form, configuration, decoration, colour pattern) must be new worldwide before the priority date (absolute novelty). Originality = significant features caused by the creative nature of the article's characteristics. Designs must not be solely dictated by technical function, nor include certain excluded subject-matter (e.g., architecture, unstable forms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-eligible subject matter (general exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following shall not be objects of invention/utility model patents: human cloning technologies; techniques for modifying the genetic integrity of human embryo cells; use of human embryos for industrial and commercial purposes; other solutions inconsistent with public interest and humane or moral principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inter alia discoveries, rules and methods of intellectual activities, varieties of plants and animals and biological methods for producing them (except microbiological methods and products produced by such methods) shall not be deemed inventions. Note: methods of treatment by surgery or therapy and diagnostic methods practised on the human or animal body are available for invention patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty — what destroys novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: A document is considered novelty destroying if it discloses all features of the claimed invention or the entirety of the significant features of the utility model/design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For inventions novelty is absolute (worldwide). For utility models novelty is relative as described above. Novelty must also be assessed against 'elder rights'—unpublished pending patent or design applications filed earlier with Rospatent by others and later published, and earlier patented subject-matter in Russia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace period for inventor disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: For inventions and utility models there is a grace period of 6 months prior to the filing date concerning disclosure by the inventor, applicant or someone who obtained the information from them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 6-month grace period also applies to industrial designs concerning disclosure of information by the author/applicant or those who obtained it from them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elder rights (effect of earlier-filed pending domestic applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claimed subject matter must be novel over 'elder rights'—unpublished pending patent/design applications filed with the Russian Patent Office by others before the priority date (if later published) and earlier Russian patents/designs with prior time rank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elder rights can destroy novelty even if the earlier application was unpublished at the claimant's priority date, provided it has earlier filing date/time rank.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventiveness (non-obviousness) standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventiveness means that for the specialist the invention does not obviously ensue from the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility models are exempt from the inventiveness requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability standard
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention is deemed industrially applicable if it can be used in industry, agriculture, public health and other branches of economy or in the social sphere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often grounds for objection in substantive examination (especially in chemistry) concern insufficient exemplification of feasibility and purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms of protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective exclusive-right terms: 20 years from filing for an invention; 10 years from filing for a utility model (may be extended up to 3 years); 15 years from filing for an industrial design (may be extended up to 10 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term extension available for invention patents relating to medicines, pesticides or agrochemical substances that require market authorization: extension equals elapsed period from filing to first market authorization minus five years. Effective term extensions may apply to independent claims relating to compounds/compositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent eligibility limits for utility models and designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility model patents are not granted for processes, substances, micro-organism strains, animal or plant cell cultures or other products not considered apparatus. No protection as a utility model for solutions concerning only appearance aimed at aesthetic needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design patents are not granted for solutions exclusively due to technical function, objects of architecture/immovable structures, or objects of unstable form (fluids, gases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority date and priority-claim deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority date is the filing date of the first patent application in a Paris-Convention member state covering the subject matter. A subsequent Russian invention/utility model application may claim that priority if filed within 12 months (6 months for design patents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First-to-file system applies: if there are two applications for the same invention the patent is granted to the one who filed first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing formalities and representation for foreign applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign companies must use a patent attorney registered with the Russian Patent Office to handle filing. The request to grant a patent must be filed in Russian; Russian translation of application materials can be filed with the request or within the 31-month PCT national-phase term (or within two months after a notification, extendable up to 10 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant is not notified by Rospatent within six months after filing they may file abroad without further approval. Applicant may request an examination for presence of state secret to accelerate proceedings to allow earlier foreign filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routes to obtain patent protection (national, Eurasian, PCT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three main routes: file a national Russian application with Rospatent; file a regional Eurasian patent application designating Russia with the Eurasian Patent Office; designate/elect Russia in a PCT application and enter national phase before Rospatent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eurasian route currently (at time of publication) about twice as expensive as the Russian route if one is only interested in Russia. PCT national phase entry to Russia: 31 months from earliest priority date to enter national phase; some Administrative Regulation requirements (e.g., dependent-claims grouping) do not apply for PCT applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: State secret first-filing requirement for Russian-origin inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: If an invention is created in the Russian Federation, a patent application has to be filed first in Russia because an examination for state secret is required before filing abroad; failure to comply results in administrative liability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement applies only to applications filed by Russian applicants/co-applicants. If Rospatent has not notified applicant within six months after filing, the applicant may file abroad without further approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing and temporary protection for invention applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications are published 18 months after filing date (national) or 18 months after expiry of the 31-month term (PCT). An invention patent application enjoys temporary legal protection from publication of the application until publication of information on patent issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For illegal use during the temporary protection period the infringer shall pay monetary compensation to the patent owner after issuance of the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination procedure for invention patents (two-step)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a two-step procedure: formal examination and substantive examination. Applicant must request substantive examination within 3 years of filing, otherwise application is deemed withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FIPS performs formal and substantive examination. Publication occurs during the process (see above). Failure to file substantive examination request within 3 years leads to withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination procedure for utility model patents (formal only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility model applications undergo a formal examination only (unity, completeness, whether the claimed solution is protectable as a utility model). If no ground for rejection is found, a patent certificate is issued (10 years from filing, extendable up to 3 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No substantive examination on novelty/inventiveness for utility models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel filing and transformation between invention and utility model applications
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not allowed that two patents (one for an invention and one for a utility model identical thereto) having the same applicant and same priority are granted. The second patent will be granted only after the applicant has renounced the first patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Until publication of the invention application but not later than the issuance decision date, an invention application can be transformed into a utility model application; likewise a utility model application can be transformed into an invention application until the decision date on issuance of the utility model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments during prosecution — 'essence of the invention' test
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant is entitled to amend application documents unless the essence of the invention is changed. Additional materials change the essence if they comprise features intended to be included in claims but not disclosed in the priority documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative Regulation refers to the original application documents (not the priority documents). Careful consideration required because amendments may trigger fees (amendment fee if not filed within two months after filing date) and possible claim fees if number of claims exceeds thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims structure restrictions and claim-fee consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim set should not comprise a multiple-dependent claim forming the basis for a further multiple-dependent claim. If it does, applicants may substitute multiple references by single references; excess claims may incur claim fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment strategies (e.g., preserving feature combinations by adding dependent claims each with single reference) may increase costs. In nullity actions patent owner can amend independent claims by incorporating features from dependent claims or description; in infringement proceedings only independent claims are relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design application required documents
rubrics_metrics.description: A design patent application must comprise a written description of the design, a list of significant features (similar to a claim), a set of images of the article and a request for grant in order to obtain a filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An industrial design application may relate to one design or a group of interrelated designs forming a united creative concept (unity of industrial design).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for nullity of patents (invention, utility model, design)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds: (1) the claimed subject matter does not comply with patentability conditions; (2) granted claims or list of significant features contain features beyond original disclosure; (3) patent granted although several applications for identical subject-matter with same priority exist; (4) patent issued indicating inventor/owner who is not such or missing indication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nullity based on grounds 1-3 may be filed with the CPD at Rospatent by any legal entity or individual without needing to show particular legal interest; there is no time limit for grounds 1-3. Ground 4 must be filed with the Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal procedure against Rospatent decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: If Rospatent issues a decision on rejection, grant or deeming the application withdrawn, an appeal may be filed with the Chamber for Patent Disputes (CPD) within six months from receipt of the decision (or from receipt of prior-art copies if requested within 2 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If CPD or Rospatent decision is negative, applicant may file for invalidation of an unlawful state-organ decision with Arbitration Court within 3 months after issuance; appeals thereafter have specified shorter deadlines at successive courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court proceedings and appellate structure (civil/patent disputes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent litigation is tried by Arbitration Courts (for disputes between legal persons) comprising four levels, and Courts of General Jurisdiction (if one party is a natural person) comprising three levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines and modes for appeals: request for invalidation of unlawful state organ decision filed within 3 months; appeals to appellation instance within 1 month, cassation within 2 months, higher instances thereafter with specified deadlines. Typical durations: first instance Arbitration 6-10 months; second instance 2-3 months; cassation 3-4 months; Higher Arbitration Court 1-2 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment and licensing formal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment contracts relating to a patent application or a patent must be in written form or they are invalid; assignment with respect to a patent must be registered with the Patent Office. Licensing contracts must be recorded with Rospatent to be valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment takes effect on the date of registration. Foreign owners should be aware that compulsory-licensing provisions may apply under the Civil Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory licence conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Simple compulsory licences may be granted by court decision where the patentee, after expiration of 4 years from grant (3 years for utility model), has not sufficiently exploited the patent without good reason and refuses to conclude a licence on terms meeting prevailing practice; the patentee insufficiently exploits the patent if failing to meet domestic demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compulsory licences can also be granted for inventions representing an important technical achievement and having significant economic advantages over a holder's earlier invention (dependent patents) to permit exploitation of dependent patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee (service) inventions rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention/utility model/design created by an employee in the course of duties or specific assignment is a service invention; attribution rights belong to the employee but exclusive right and right to obtain a patent are owned by employer unless contract states otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If within 4 months after written notification the employer does not file an application, assign the right, or notify that information is secret, the right to obtain a patent belongs to the employee. If employer obtains patent or keeps secret or assigns to another or fails to obtain patent for reasons within employer's control, employee is entitled to remuneration—amount/terms by contract or court; government may set minimum rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of patent-infringing acts
rubrics_metrics.description: Without authorisation, no one may exploit the patent: make, use, offer to sell, sell, import, other introduction into civil-law transactions or storage for such purposes of a product where the invention/utility model is used or an article where the design is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also includes performing these actions with a product obtained by a patented method (product-by-process presumed identical unless proven otherwise) and implementing methods that use the invention, including automatic apparatus implementations. An invention/utility model is deemed used if product contains each feature of an independent claim or an equivalent known in the field prior to the infringing act. An industrial design is used if article contains all significant features reflected in images and list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible defences to infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions not deemed infringement include private (non-commercial) use; carrying out scientific research or experiments; importation/offer/sale/storage of a product previously introduced into Russian civil-law circulation by the patent holder or with their permission (national exhaustion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These defenses can be raised depending on facts; private and experimental uses are explicitly listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statute of limitations for infringement claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The statute of limitations for patent infringement is three years starting from the date the patent holder knew or should have known of the infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims outside this window are time-barred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement options (administrative, civil, criminal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owners have three main enforcement options once infringement is discovered: administrative enforcement (including border measures), civil enforcement, and criminal enforcement; for complex technical questions civil enforcement is most important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice depends on facts; administrative can give quick seizure and fines, criminal requires proof of major damage, civil provides monetary relief and injunctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative enforcement specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Code of Administrative Offences unauthorized use of a patent entails fines (natural person 1,500–2,000 RUB; legal entity 30,000–100,000 RUB) and seizure of infringing goods; administrative cases are investigated by militia or customs and tried by courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-monopoly action can be brought under the Law on Protection of Competition for unlawful use of IP, potentially ordering transfer of infringer's profits to state budget; administrative proceedings are carried out where the infringing act occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing a patent infringement statement of claim (evidence needs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Crucial preparation issues: obtain sample of infringing product; for chemical products get independent laboratory analysis; collect evidence that product was introduced into civil-law transactions; translate and certify all foreign-language documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sending a warning letter is not a prerequisite and may provoke counter-actions (e.g., infringer filing a patent). Suit generally filed where infringer is located.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary injunctions and evidence preservation (preliminary security measures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plaintiff can request Arbitration Court to stop infringing acts and seize infringing products before suit (preliminary security measures). Prerequisites: show (1) lawful rights being infringed or imminent infringement; (2a) infringement will result in significant damage or (2b) not taking measures would make execution of decision more difficult or impossible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plaintiff must provide security (local bank account or guarantee). Plaintiff must institute legal proceedings within 15 days after court issues preliminary measures or measures are terminated. Practically preliminary measures have rarely been granted because judge cannot rely on expert opinion in preliminary proceedings, though security measures during a lawsuit have been granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of expert opinions in court proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: In patent cases courts generally order an expert opinion. The party requesting an expert proposes a specific independent expert (name and qualification) and a questionnaire and agrees remuneration; the court decides which expert to appoint and may appoint a team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expert evidence plays a central role in technical disputes; parties should prepare proposed experts and agreed remuneration to expedite appointment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial procedures, typical timelines and enforceability
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing, court serves defendant; preliminary hearing usually within two months; main hearing follows; first-instance decision becomes enforceable if not appealed within one month or appeal is dismissed. Average durations: first instance Arbitration Court approx. 6–10 months; second-instance 2–3 months; cassation 3–4 months; Higher Arbitration Court 1–2 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court fees for Arbitration instances are relatively low (e.g., 2,000 RUB first instance, 1,000 RUB for later instances at time of publication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal enforcement thresholds and penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Unauthorized use of a patent is a criminal offence if major damage is caused (approx. 50,000 RUB depending on circumstances). Penalties include fines up to 200,000 RUB, fine equal to income for up to 18 months, compulsory work 180–240 hours, or imprisonment up to two years. Aggravated penalties for group/organized crime include higher fines, arrest, or imprisonment up to five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criminal cases are investigated by Ministry of Interior and tried by Courts of General Jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages and monetary relief
rubrics_metrics.description: If infringement is proven, patent owner may demand actual damages (expenditures incurred to reinstate rights) and lost profit or alternatively compensation equal to the infringer's profits. Losing party must reimburse legal costs for experts, testimonies, etc., and the other party's attorney fees to a reasonable amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts calculate damages based on evidence of lost profit or infringer's gains; reasonable reimbursement of litigation costs is available to prevailing party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary legal protection and compensation for use before grant
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention patent application enjoys temporary legal protection from publication of the application until publication of information on issuance of the patent; for illegal use during this period the infringer shall pay monetary compensation to the patent owner after issuance of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a route to monetary relief for acts occurring after publication but before grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nullity petition filing rights and time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Any legal entity or individual may file a nullity action on grounds 1–3 with the CPD at Rospatent; petitioner need not show legal interest and there is no time limit. Ground 4 (wrong inventor/owner) must be filed with the Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nullity actions can be initiated at any time for the listed grounds; strategic use of CPD actions is common in validity challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of claim wording and equivalents in infringement analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention or utility model is deemed to be used if a product contains each feature of an independent claim or a feature equivalent thereto (a feature that had become known in the given field before the infringing act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners should draft claims carefully; equivalence doctrine can broaden scope in infringement analyses; independent claims determine infringement in proceedings.
